title: Give every wagon a declared, stable URN and the plan/<wagon-slug>/ layout

values: file of a wagon's own file set
facts.note: The trigger is a wagon itself, not any file that mentions one. A wagon is identified by the file that defines it, typically its wagon manifest. The wagon's own file set is the files that belong to it under the documented layout. Files that only describe or reference a wagon do not count: docs, trains or components that cite its URN. Identification is content-based and works wherever the definition sits, including outside plan/. A classifier for wagon definitions is needed. Until one exists, an LLM judges.
This is a discovery hint only, NOT a required filter. A wagon definition found outside plan/ still fires the rule, and that misplacement is itself a layout violation.
Any of these operations on a wagon definition or its own file set can add, change or drop the URN, or break the layout.

values: wagon URN declared, changed or removed
wagon's own files added, removed or relocated
facts.note: A diff-level observer is needed. It compares the wagon's declared URN before and after the change, and it compares the wagon's file set with the plan/<wagon-slug>/ layout. Until it exists, an LLM judges.
Planning tasks that author, restructure or reorganise wagons.

fires: A planner creates a new wagon, wherever its definition is placed.
A planner edits, renames or moves an existing wagon, or edits its declared URN.
A planner adds, removes or relocates files of a wagon's own file set. This includes a layout-only change.
A wagon definition is found outside plan/<wagon-slug>/.
A wagon definition has no declared URN.
doesNotFire: A file only describes or references a wagon, for example a doc, train or component that cites a wagon URN, and no wagon definition or wagon file set is created, moved or modified.
The change touches only non-wagon artifacts, such as source code, tests, or plan files that define no wagon.

given: The change creates or modifies a wagon, meaning its defining manifest or its own file set, wherever it is located. Files that merely mention a wagon do not count.
when: The planner creates, edits, renames, moves or reorganises that wagon.
then: The wagon declares a stable URN (wagon_urn), and that URN does not change when the wagon is edited, renamed or moved.
prefer: Keep a wagon's existing URN when you edit, rename or move it.
Give a new wagon a URN in the grammar defined by planner.wagon.urn-naming.

Place every wagon under plan/<wagon-slug>/ with the documented file layout (wagon_layout). This is required by the same source statement. Derive the slug as planner.wagon.logical-vs-filesystem-naming specifies.
avoid: A wagon with no declared URN, or with a URN derived from something that changes over time.
Rewriting a wagon's URN as part of other edits.
A wagon that lives outside plan/<wagon-slug>/, or whose file set departs from the documented layout.
why: Trains and components refer to a wagon by its URN, and the URN must resolve to a real wagon at a predictable location. A missing or changing URN, or a misplaced wagon, breaks those references.
evidence: Each wagon touched by the change declares exactly one URN (in its defining manifest), and for an existing wagon that URN is the same before and after the change.
Each wagon touched by the change lives under plan/<wagon-slug>/ and its file set matches the documented layout. This is a mandatory part of this rule.
The disposition is documentation-only (severity 3), so a reviewer confirms compliance by inspection. No automated gate is implied.
verifier_detail: Severity 3, disposition documentation-only: this is a review guideline, not a strict gate.
Term wagon_urn: a wagon's stable URN.
Term wagon_layout: the plan/<wagon-slug>/ directory layout.

Unit of check: the wagon, not each associated file. Identify a wagon by its defining manifest, the file that declares the wagon. Check the URN once per wagon on that definition. Check layout on the wagon's own file set. Do not treat docs, trains or components that only reference a wagon URN as wagons. plan/** is only a discovery hint and must never restrict detection, so wagon definitions outside plan/ are still found and reported as layout violations.

Original statement: Wagons declare a stable URN and live under plan/<wagon-slug>/ with the documented file layout.

splitSuggestion.then: Every wagon lives under plan/<wagon-slug>/ and follows the documented file layout (wagon_layout). Disposition: documentation-only, severity 3.

additions.text: The source combines two independently checkable obligations: a stable URN and the plan/<wagon-slug>/ layout. `then` carries the URN obligation. In this rule the layout obligation stays mandatory and unconditional through prefer[2], avoid[2] and evidence[1]. A separate convention, planner.wagon.layout, could carry it later. That would need an explicit transfer, and the layout stays required here until then.
additions.justification: Rule 2 requires one obligation in `then`. The auditor requires layout to remain mandatory with no expiry condition.

additions.text: Activation facts plus fires and doesNotFire cases. A wagon is identified by its defining manifest and its own file set, not by files that merely reference it. plan/** is a non-required discovery hint.
additions.justification: The source has no activation section. The auditor required detection that does not depend on location but is not broadened to mere references.

additions.text: prefer[0], avoid[1]: keep the URN on edit, rename or move. prefer[1], prefer[2]: pointers to planner.wagon.urn-naming for URN grammar and to planner.wagon.logical-vs-filesystem-naming for slug derivation.
additions.justification: These spell out 'stable'. The pointers come from graph.json 'requires' edges. No grammar is invented here.

additions.text: Engineering reason: trains and components reference wagons by URN, and the URN must resolve to a real wagon at a predictable location.
additions.justification: The source has no rationale. This comes from the graph.json edges planner.component.urn and planner.train.scope.

additions.text: Per-wagon inspection evidence, plus the unit-of-check detection criteria in verifier_detail[3].
additions.justification: The source has no evidence section. These follow directly from the statement and the documentation-only disposition, and they add no exceptions.

trace.note: The name 'Wagon URN + layout' is reflected in the title, which covers both halves, and is kept verbatim in audit.
The URN obligation is in `then`. The layout obligation is unconditionally mandatory via prefer[2], avoid[2] and evidence[1]. Both are checked per wagon.
